intro.title: useCallback for Stable References
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple counter app with buttons that log messages to the console. You'll learn how to use the React useCallback hook to create stable function references, preventing unnecessary re-renders of child components. The main technologies involved are React functional components, the useCallback hook, and event handlers in JavaScript. This will help you understand how to optimize performance by memoizing functions, especially when passing them as props to child components.
intro.usecase: In real applications, useCallback is essential for preventing unnecessary re-renders in complex interactive interfaces. For example, dashboard components with multiple filtering controls, data visualization tooltips, or sortable tables all benefit from stable callback references. When users interact with search filters in e-commerce sites or adjust settings panels in analytics tools, useCallback ensures that event handlers don't trigger wasteful re-renders of child components. This pattern is particularly valuable in data-intensive applications like financial dashboards or project management tools where performance directly impacts user experience.
